newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JOBBERS UP SENTRACHEM, EYE DOW'S RESPONSE.
newsitem.headline: JOBBERS UP SENTRACHEM, EYE DOW'S RESPONSE.

text.p: Shares in South African chemicals firm Sentrachem Ltd rose on Tuesday driven by expectations that U.S. chemical giant Dow Chemical Co could better its purchase offer, dealers said.

By about 1155 GMT Sentrachem was up 25 cents at 10.50 rand, a price at which Dow offered to buy each Sentrachem share before members of its board of directors, who are not directors of its major shareholder Sankorp Ltd, rejected it earlier on Tuesday.
The members of the board said 2.074 billion rand bid for Sentrachem did not adequately represent the value of Sentrachem's businesses.
Dealers said jobbers hoping to make a profit if Dow increased its offer were pouring into Sentrachem shares which started to climb from 792 cents on August 4.
"I think guys now reckon there could be a bigger offer and I think that's why the share is going up," one dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said.
"There are just jobbers buying here hoping for a better offer from Dow than 10.50 rand in order to make some profits if Dow comes back with a higher offer, lets say of 11.00 rand," the dealer added.
"I'm sure that there are guys just getting out now because there's uncertainty on what's going on and on what the price should be," the dealer added.
Dow has already sealed an agreement with Sankorp Ltd, which holds 38.74 percent of Sentrachem, to accept and recommend the offer at the initial price.
